predecessors.name: Pagan Kingdom
predecessors.text: the Shan Hills and the northern uplands that left Pagan as the Mongols overran it in 1287

successors.name: Toungoo Empire
successors.text: the Shan outline of 1563: Bayinnaung's vassal Shan states, 'Subjugation by the Taungoo dynasty: 1557'

ledger.x: 1287: the Shan principalities rise as Pagan falls.
1388: Si Lunfa surrenders to the Ming ('Si Lunfa surrendered in 1388') after a larger punitive expedition; he invaded Ava in 1393, was deposed in 1397 and restored in 1398.

1437: the Luchuan-Pingmian campaigns begin with Si Renfa's push into Ming-held land: 'Si Renfa continued to expand, invading Nandian in 1437'; the Ming then 'prepared a campaign', the first sent in 1438 (one Ming army destroyed) and the second in 1441, which besieged the capital.
1442: Möng Mao's capital falls to the Ming and Si Renfa flees to Möng Yang ('Möng Mao's capital fell in 1442').
1444: the Ming take the Yunnan lands of Möng Mao.
1449: the fourth campaign ends in a peace treaty with Silu, a son of Si Renfa, and 'a boundary stone was set up on the Irrawaddy'.
14 March 1527: the Confederation of Shan States sacks Ava.
1533: the Confederation takes Prome: 'The enlarged Confederation extended its authority down to Prome (Pyay) in 1533 by defeating their erstwhile ally Prome Kingdom', its ally of 1527.
1545: Toungoo pushes the Confederation back to Pagan.
1556: Bayinnaung turns on the Shan states.
March 1557: most of the cis-Salween Shan states are Toungoo's.
1563: the last Shan states, Kengtung and the Chinese Shan states, come under Toungoo.

wars.name: Möng Mao raids on Sagaing and Pinya
wars.outcome: Maw forces breached northern Sagaing in 1342, raided in 1356-57, 1358-59 and 1362-63, and sacked Sagaing in April 1364 and Pinya in May 1364; Thado Minbya took Pinya in September 1364 and founded Ava in 1365.

wars.name: Ming campaigns against Si Lunfa
wars.outcome: Möng Mao attacked Jingdong in 1385, defeated a Ming expedition in 1387 and surrendered in 1388.

wars.name: Luchuan-Pingmian campaigns
wars.outcome: Four Ming campaigns: 1438 a Ming army destroyed, 1442 the capital falls, 1444 it falls again and the core is partitioned, 1449 peace and a boundary stone on the Irrawaddy.

wars.name: Shan conquest of Ava
wars.outcome: The Confederation sacked Ava (14 March 1527) and ruled Upper Burma until 1555.

wars.name: Toungoo-Ava War (1538-45)
wars.outcome: Toungoo 'seized up to Pagan (Bagan)' from the Confederation by 1545.

wars.name: Toungoo conquest of the Shan States
wars.outcome: Most cis-Salween states by March 1557, Hsenwi's tribute on 26 July 1558, Kengtung before 16 December 1562, nominal suzerainty over the Chinese Shan states by 1563.

certainty.note: A ring of principalities (möng) with no surveyed or treaty frontiers; the nearest fixed line is the boundary stone set up on the Irrawaddy in 1449, a marker on a river, not a border.
